body: Same specimen as run-jargon-breaker-20261005-amping, plus JayArr's context (2026-10-07): the remark usually came from male peers, about getting 'emotional' in how he responds to treatment by or of women, which he took as their assumption of how a 'man' is supposed to act. J4 'emotional': sense (b), feeling overriding sense, now fixed as 'showing feeling where a man is expected not to'; conf 75. J4/J5 'when it comes to women': now two named referents, treatment BY women and treatment OF women, so two situations stated as one. J7 plain version: 'You're not acting the way a man is supposed to when women are involved.' That is clearly less comfortable than 'you get emotional', so by J7's test the opacity does work: it enforces a norm while sounding like a description of a mood. VERDICT: AIMED (about the language; no claim about anyone's intent; I0 at most: the effect of the phrasing). Was IMPRECISION without context. FINDING ABOUT THE TOOL: the same sentence returns a different verdict once the ruler is known, so a verdict on a context-free specimen is provisional by construction. NULL: J1, J2, J3, J8 (not run), J9 (stress not recoverable).
plain: Re-run of the Jargon Breaker on 'emotional' with JayArr's context added: the verdict moves from IMPRECISION toward AIMED. The missing ruler turns out to be a norm for how a man should act.
